evidence.summary: Inspected project instructions, PostgreSQL/native ownership contract and the implemented extension. Existing host watcher owns process liveness and now idle host prompting; store owns read-only eligibility via session/execution generation and native hook owns claims. Existing boundaries are reused, no new broker/credential/service/storage engine. Prompt checks use documented installed Herdr fields and defer unavailable identities and focused/busy targets. Herdr has no atomic idle-only submission; final state race is explicitly retained, no fabricated guarantee. Alternatives are documented: manual-only no-change fails requested automation, timed uncertain retry risks duplicate prompts, holding the lock through submission would collide with the hook. Full integration/check plus real deployment trial required; no migration needed.

evidence.summary: Read all changed functions and their callers. prepare_idle_wake runs under the existing nonblocking session flock; it asks read-only readiness, checks process/socket/native identity and Herdr state twice, then persists a per-delivery/execution uncertain marker. It releases the flock before prompt submission; the native hook can claim under its own flock and clears the marker only when native inbox context is emitted. A fresh process reads persisted state; no shared mutable object crosses processes. The preparation record shares only local objects that are not subsequently mutated during submission; completion rereads state before conditional status replacement. Herdr subprocesses have four-second timeouts, registry calls retain existing timeouts. Single watcher owns sequential ticks; no new concurrent pool or lock order. SQL shares eligibility/hold predicates with native claims and returns at most one ID, excluding expired/offline/busy/fenced contexts. No new logical identity or schema, delivery attempt or effects during readiness. Existing profile/privacy, leases, restore fencing, native completion and all other harness behavior remain protected. Added wake-time opt-out checks for both observed and selected workspaces; hook and watcher share the existing ancestor marker semantics.

evidence.summary: Preservation review: native claims and renewals remain in the same hook path; readiness performs no writes; stale generation uses currentAgentSession; same API profile and sensitivity conditions apply; no raw transcript or credential values enter host prompts. Project exclusion markers are checked again at wake time, verified by a regression that failed before the guard and passed afterward. Named host limitations include the final observation/submission race and unknown composer drafts; no security or atomic-delivery claim. Existing manual-only behavior fails the owner-requested automation by construction; retaining it is not selected. Work is scoped to the existing single host and seven configured bindings; no throughput/latency improvement is claimed. Reversal disables idle_wakeup without resetting session or delivery state.

assertions.text: Current native delivery needs a supported boundary; the ai-newsroom test supplied a manual Herdr prompt. Installed Herdr 0.9.0 has no atomic idle-only prompt.

Use the existing watcher and a read-only eligibility query to submit one advisory host prompt, retaining uncertain attempts and leaving claims to native hooks. Recheck actual process/conversation, defer focused/unknown/busy targets and honor opt-outs. No new credentials, broker or store migration.

Disposable store/API tests and Python protocol fixtures verify eligibility, process/session selection, duplicate suppression and native claim ownership. These checks do not establish the pending production automatic-wakeup trial.

residual_risk: Herdr has no atomic idle-only prompt or composer reservation; snapshots cannot eliminate the final user/process race or prove no saved input draft. Focused panes defer. Native hooks still own delivery.
Sessions without a verified Herdr/native association retain boundary delivery. Gateway conversations without an interactive idle process are not targets.
A lost host response stays uncertain and suppressed; a real native boundary or operator investigation is required.
Nonmaterial: recurring change evidence when available. This is a newly required feature in the existing owner, not a restructuring justified by churn.
Nonmaterial: workload evidence for optimization. No performance optimization or measured latency guarantee is claimed.
